description:
## Goal
A value of a concrete type that implements a protocol IS a member of that protocol's type. Today it is not: a protocol type and its implementers are disjoint opaques, so a concrete receiver flowing through a generic protocol-typed parameter graduates to any, taking the element type with it. Fix the protocol TYPE MODEL so the relation holds by construction. Big effect, localized change.

## Root (read end-to-end, to_list(1..3))
1. A protocol's t(a) is minted as a BARE OPAQUE 'protocol::Enumerable.t' (resolve.rs:104 NominalKind::Opaque) that (a) drops the parameter a -- the opaque carries no structure for it -- and (b) is DISJOINT from every impl target (impl-target::Range etc., distinct opaque brands).
2. Because they are disjoint, intersect(Enumerable.t, Range) = empty. So:
   - A concrete receiver flowing into an Enumerable.t param only survives by the refine_contract_inputs empty-intersection FALLBACK (keeps the arg) -- it is never RELATED to the protocol type, and a is never bound.
   - When a bridge fn (Enum.reduce/3, reverse/1, to_list/1) is analyzed with a non-concrete (opaque/any) receiver, resolve_protocol_call's protocol_receiver_target_overlaps finds NO arm (opaque disjoint from all targets) -> dispatch unresolved -> the call earns any.
3. Cascade (traced): reverse(Range) returns the bridge reduce/3 accumulator b; with the element a erased to any, b graduates to any; to_list = reverse(reverse(enumerable)) feeds that any back into the outer reverse -> reduce <- reverse[any]. The any then floods arithmetic (f98.11) and is the any-axis of the f98.5/f98.6 over-monomorphization. (The int|float axis was f98.8.)
4. Secondary: module_impl_target_ty_with (world.rs:3070) builds struct impl targets with vec![any; field_count] -- the f98.8 any-fields default again, at the DISPATCH target.

## Required work (localized)
- resolve.rs (~104): a protocol domain type must not be a bare disjoint opaque. Model it as a BOUND its impls satisfy -- carrying the parameter a -- so impl-target types are members/subtypes and intersect(impl, Protocol.t) is the impl (non-empty), and matching a concrete receiver against Protocol.t(a) BINDS a to the receiver's element.
- Relate impl targets to the protocol bound (defimpl registration / module_impl_target_ty): an impl target carries the protocol membership so dispatch overlap and contract narrowing work by construction, not by empty-fallback.
- resolve_protocol_call (semantic.rs:1226) / refine_protocol_target_inputs (1738): bind a to the impl's concrete element and propagate it to the return, so the bridge return stays concrete instead of graduating.
- module_impl_target_ty_with (world.rs:3070): honor declared struct field types for the dispatch target too (reuse the fz-f98.8 declared-type path), not vec![any].

## Checks
- to_list(1..3) range elements stay int and the bridge return stays [int]; the top-union/any reduce/3 & reverse/1 activations disappear.
- fz-f98.9 graduated-any count drops sharply (this is the dominant cluster).
- Full lib + matrix at baseline (no new failures); no protocol behavior regressions.

## Not the problem
Not a bridge patch, not a convergence tweak, not an operator fix -- those are downstream of the disjoint-opaque model. The provider-boundary any (function_is_provider_boundary) is the only LEGITIMATE earned any and is unaffected.
title: Enumerable protocol boundary erases element type to any (t(a) -> any)
